hetumavakaḍḍhayitvā.meaning_2: having drawn forth the cause; having extracted the reason
hetumavakaḍḍhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of a compound verb (hetuṃ + avakaḍḍhati). Written as one word (hetum- for hetuṃ) before the vowel. The reading may be a variant for hetuṃ avakaḍḍhayitvā.
hetumavakaḍḍhayitvā.translation_2: By drawing forth the cause, this conveying is the Conveying of the Requisite.

volokayate.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative with vi-ava-; the text has the singular -yate for -yati. In the Nettippakaraṇa it describes mental scrutiny, 'one contemplates mentally'.
volokayate.translation_2: One contemplates mentally: that indeed they call the Plotting of Directions.

disalocanena.meaning_2: with the eye of the directions; by the direction-seeing; by the Plotting of Directions
disalocanena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of disā + locanena (instrumental of disalocana). In the Nettippakaraṇa it is a technical term rendered 'Plotting of Directions'. Variant disalocanato in the parallel sentence.
disalocanena.translation_2: 21. Having contemplated by the Plotting of Directions, what then lifts up;

saṅkhipiya.meaning_2: having collected; having summed up; having condensed
saṅkhipiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Gerund in -iya from saṃ + √khip. The PEU also records an adjective saṅkhipiya (= saṅkhipitabba). Here it is indeclinable, governing aṅkusena, and precedes niddise in the verse.
saṅkhipiya.example_2: Saṅkhipiya aṅkusena hi, nayehi tīhi niddise suttaṃ.
saṅkhipiya.translation_2: And having collected by the Hook, one should demonstrate the discourse by the three guidelines.

vipañcayati.meaning_2: expands; elaborates; explains in detail; diversifies
vipañcayati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third singular present in the text, paired with ugghaṭeti (condenses) and vitthāreti (details). The PEU analysis vi + paci + ṇaya + ti is uncertain; the root may rather be √pac with the causative sign.
vipañcayati.example_1: tattha bhagavā akkharehi ca padehi ca ugghaṭeti, byañjanehi ca ākārehi ca vipañcayati, niruttīhi ca niddesehi ca vitthāreti.
vipañcayati.example_2: Tattha bhagavā akkharehi ca padehi ca ugghaṭeti [ugghāṭeti (sī.)], byañjanehi ca ākārehi ca vipañcayati, niruttīhi ca niddesehi ca vitthāreti.
vipañcayati.translation_2: Herein, the Blessed One condenses by letters and by terms, he expands by expressions and by modes, he details by linguistics and by demonstrations.

vipañcanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Nettippakaraṇa it names the middle stage of exposition, between condensing and detailing. Related to vipañcana.
vipañcanā.example_1: tattha ugghaṭanā ādi, vipañcanā majjhe, vitthāraṇā pariyosānaṃ.
vipañcanā.example_2: Tattha ugghaṭanā [ugghāṭanā (sī.)] ādi, vipañcanā majjhe, vitthāraṇā pariyosānaṃ.
vipañcanā.translation_2: Herein, condensing is the beginning, expanding is the middle, and detailing is the end.

ugghaṭīyanto.meaning_2: being opened; opening up; being made clear
ugghaṭīyanto.root_base: √ghaṭ + *e > ghaṭe (caus); ghaṭe + ya > ghaṭīya (pass); u + ghaṭīya + a > ugghaṭīya (irreg)
ugghaṭīyanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle masculine nominative singular. Refers to the dhamma-vinaya being opened or explained. Transliteration: ugghaṭīyanto.
ugghaṭīyanto.example_1: soyaṃ dhammavinayo ugghaṭīyanto ugghaṭitaññūpuggalaṃ vineti, tena naṃ āhu “ādikalyāṇo”ti.

vipañcīyanto.meaning_2: ripens; brings to maturity; develops; instructs
vipañcīyanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Lemma uncertain: the text has the present participle vipañcīyanto, which looks passive in form (vi + √pac + ya + māna). The causative vipañcayati is inferred from the context 'vipañcīyanto ... vineti' (matures the person ripe for maturity and trains them). Nom. sg. masc. of the present participle; the headword could alternatively be taken as a passive participle stem vipañcīyanta.
vipañcīyanto.example_1: vipañcīyanto vipañcitaññūpuggalaṃ vineti, tena naṃ āhu “majjhekalyāṇo”ti.

atocetaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ato (therefore) + cetaṃ (and that; or emphatic). Appears to mean 'therefore this' in the sentence; sandhi resolution and meaning are uncertain.
atocetaṃ.example_1: Parisuddhanti nimmalaṃ sabbamalāpagataṃ pariyodātaṃ upaṭṭhitaṃ sabbavisesānaṃ, idaṃ vuccati tathāgatapadaṃitipi tathāgatanisevitaṃitipi tathāgatārañjitaṃitipi, atocetaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paññāyati.
atocetaṃ.translation_1: ‘Pure’ means immaculate, with all stains removed, bright, established for all distinctions. This is called ‘a Perfect One’s footprint,’ and ‘something used by a Perfect One,’ and ‘something marked by a Perfect One.’ For that reason, this spiritual life is recognized.

uppādiyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present; causative sense 'causes to arise'. The text has the negative na uppādiyati; the related form anuppādiyamānā is a present participle.
uppādiyati.example_1: so idhappamādamanuyutto viharati pamatto, sukke dhamme na uppādiyati, tassa te anuppādiyamānā nappakāsanti, yathāha bhagavā—

abhilimpati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular present in the text, in an interrogative sentence.

abhilitto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used in the passive sense 'clung to' (as in PEU). In the sentence it modifies loko and describes how the world is attached to craving. The root is given as √lip (smear), with past participle abhilitta; the root_base is uncertain.
abhilitto.example_1: sāyaṃ taṇhā āsattibahulassa puggalassa “evaṃ abhijappā”ti karitvā tattha loko abhilitto nāma bhavati, tena ca tatiyassa padassa visajjanā yuttā.

odhaso.meaning_2: by a portion; by share; partially; in part
odhaso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Formed with the suffix -so from odhi; glossed in PEU as 'by a portion or share'. Used adverbially in the sentence with muccati ('is released in part').
odhaso.example_1: tattha loko odhaso kadāci karahaci dukkhadukkhatāya muccati.

cittasahabhūni.meaning_2: arising together with the mind; coexistent with mind
cittasahabhūni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter nominative plural in the text, agreeing with pañcindriyāni. Qualifies mental factors that arise and cease with consciousness.
cittasahabhūni.example_1: pañcindriyāni kusalāni cittasahabhūni citte uppajjamāne uppajjanti, citte nirujjhamāne nirujjhanti.

nibbattiyati.meaning_2: is produced; is brought forth; arises
nibbattiyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of nibbattayati (causative), 3rd singular; the sentence has nibbattayati with nibbattiyati as an alternative. Some analyses take it as a passive-like form 'is produced'.
nibbattiyati.example_1: Nāmarūpamapi ahetu appaccayaṃ punabbhavaṃ na nibbattayati [nibbattiyati (ka.)].
nibbattiyati.translation_1: No name-and-form occurs in a new existence without cause and without condition.

pavicinitabbaṃ.meaning_2: should be investigated; should be examined; should be considered
pavicinitabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle in -tabba from pavicinati. Neuter nominative singular agreeing with suttaṃ; the text has suttañca pavicinitabbaṃ.

pavicetabbaṃ.meaning_2: to be examined; to be investigated; to be analysed
pavicetabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle in the neuter nominative singular, agreeing with suttaṃ; sometimes analysed as pavicinātabba.

sampahula.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A variant reading (ka.) of sambahula in the passage on the four mahāpadesā; the text reads sambahulattherā, 'several elders'. The PEU derives it from saṃ + pa + hū + la, but here it is best taken as a compound.
sampahula.example_1: Cattāro mahāpadesā buddhāpadeso saṅghāpadeso sambahulattherāpadeso [sampahula …(ka.)] ekattherāpadeso.
sampahula.translation_1: The four Principal Appeals to Authority are: the appeal to the Enlightened One as authority, the appeal to a community as authority, the appeal to several elders as authority, and the appeal to a single elder as authority.

kismīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kismiṃ (locative of ka) and the quotative iti; paired with kathasmīti in the set phrase vicikicchā kathaṃkathāsallaṃ.
kismīti.example_1: atha ca pana me kismīti kathasmīti vicikicchā kathaṅkathāsallaṃ cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassatīti na yujjati desanā, vicikicchā kathaṅkathāsallaṃ pahānaṃ abbhatthaṃ gacchatīti yujjati desanā.
kismīti.example_2: Atha ca pana me kismīti kathasmīti vicikicchā kathaṃkathāsallaṃ cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassatīti na yujjati desanā, vicikicchā kathaṃkathāsallaṃ pahānaṃ abbhatthaṃ gacchatīti yujjati desanā.
kismīti.translation_2: But then, the teaching is not construable thus: “The barb of uncertainty and wondering, ‘What am I? How am I?’ will keep gripping my mind.” The teaching is construable thus: “The barb of uncertainty and wondering is abandoned and subsided.”

sabbadhammayāthāvaasampaṭivedhalakkhaṇā.meaning_2: having the characteristic of not penetrating the true nature of all phenomena; with the mark of failing to understand all things as they really are
sabbadhammayāthāvaasampaṭivedhalakkhaṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive compound; analysis sabbadhamma + yāthāva + asampaṭivedha + lakkhaṇa. Feminine nominative singular, agreeing with avijjā. Printed without sandhi as sabbadhammayāthāvaasampaṭivedhalakkhaṇā.

sabbadhammasampaṭivedhalakkhaṇā.meaning_2: having the characteristic of the full understanding of all things; characterised by comprehending all phenomena
sabbadhammasampaṭivedhalakkhaṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound adjective describing vijjā; feminine nominative singular agreeing with it. The parts are sabba + dhamma, sampaṭivedha (full comprehension) and lakkhaṇa (characteristic).
sabbadhammasampaṭivedhalakkhaṇā.example_1: sabbadhammasampaṭivedhalakkhaṇā vijjā, tassā sabbaṃ neyyaṃ padaṭṭhānaṃ.

vatthuavippaṭipādānalakkhaṇo.meaning_2: characterised by not misinterpreting the basis; having the characteristic of not mishandling the matter
vatthuavippaṭipādānalakkhaṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vatthu + avippaṭipādāna + lakkhaṇa + o is possible, giving lemma_1 vatthuavippaṭipādānalakkhaṇa; the si. ka. variant vatthuavippaṭipattilakkhaṇa suggests the text may read avippaṭipatti. Nom sg describing amoho in a definition-style sentence.
vatthuavippaṭipādānalakkhaṇo.example_1: Vatthuavippaṭipattilakkhaṇo [vatthuavippaṭipādānalakkhaṇo (sī. ka.)] amoho, tassa sammāpaṭipatti padaṭṭhānaṃ.
vatthuavippaṭipādānalakkhaṇo.translation_1: Non-delusion has the characteristic of not wrongly theorizing about things; its footing is right practice.

abhipatthiyanalakkhaṇā.meaning_2: having the characteristic of being desired; characterized by longing for
abhipatthiyanalakkhaṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound describing saddhā as having the characteristic of abhipatthiyana. Feminine nominative singular in the text; the headword is the compound stem in -ā.
abhipatthiyanalakkhaṇā.translation_2: Faith has the characteristic of credence; its footing is confidence-by-having-undergone (aveccapasādo).

punabbhavavirohaṇalakkhaṇā.meaning_2: having the characteristic of developing renewal of existence; with the mark of bringing about a new life
punabbhavavirohaṇalakkhaṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of punabbhava, virohaṇa and lakkhaṇa; vi + √ruh 1 would apply to virohaṇa alone. Feminine nominative singular in agreement with saṅkhārā; also read as punabbhavavirohaṇalakkhaṇā in the parallel passage.
punabbhavavirohaṇalakkhaṇā.translation_2: Volitional formations have the characteristic of developing renewal of existence; they are the footing for consciousness.

opapaccayikanibbattilakkhaṇaṃ.meaning_2: characterised by spontaneous rebirth; having the mark of arising in an spontaneous rebirth
opapaccayikanibbattilakkhaṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular neuter agreeing with viññāṇaṃ. Possibly a dvanda or bahubbīhi compound. See opapaccayika (spontaneous rebirth) + nibbatti (arising) + lakkhaṇa (mark).

opapaccayikaṃ.meaning_2: caused by rebirth (into a new existence); pertaining to rebirth; that which is a condition of rebirth
opapaccayikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it qualifies upādānaṃ (clinging) as a condition for becoming (bhavassa padaṭṭhānaṃ). Attested as an adjective with the -ika suffix; variant form opapattika.

kāyasaṃpīḷanaṃ.meaning_2: oppression of the body; bodily affliction; physical torment
kāyasaṃpīḷanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text, subject of the sentence. Formed from kāya + saṃpīḷana (saṃ + √pīḷ).
kāyasaṃpīḷanaṃ.translation_1: Suffering is oppression of body; it is the footing for mental pain.

cittasaṃpīḷanaṃ.meaning_2: torturing the mind; mental oppression; affliction of the mind
cittasaṃpīḷanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here in the neuter nominative singular, it is equated with domanassaṃ (mental pain). The related entry treats it as an adjective (ti).
cittasaṃpīḷanaṃ.translation_1: Mental pain is oppression of cognizance; it is the footing for despairing.

lakkhayati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative formation from √lakkh; the text asks 'kiṃ lakkhayati?' (what does it characterize?). In a few resolutions the manuscript may read lakkhīyati (passive) instead.

janapadaniruttāni.meaning_2: local expression; vernacular term; word used in the countryside; popular designation
janapadaniruttāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of janapadaniruttaṃ before evaṃ. Neuter plural in -āni with nominative plural agreement (sabbāni ... janapadaniruttāni); PEU gives na. Related noun janapadanirutti (fem) follows in the same sentence.
janapadaniruttāni.example_1: ayañca vuccati atthakusalo dhammakusalo byañjanakusalo niruttikusalo pubbāparakusalo desanākusalo atītādhivacanakusalo anāgatādhivacanakusalo paccuppannādhivacanakusalo itthādhivacanakusalo purisādhivacanakusalo napuṃsakādhivacanakusalo ekādhivacanakusalo anekādhivacanakusalo, evaṃ sabbāni kātabbāni janapadaniruttāni sabbā ca janapadaniruttiyo.

parimuccitukāmā.meaning_2: desiring to be freed (from); wishing to escape (from)
parimuccitukāmā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of the infinitive parimuccituṃ (from parimuccati, √muc) and kāma. Nominative plural in the text, agreeing with ye.
parimuccitukāmā.example_1: ye apāyehi parimuccitukāmā bhavissanti, te dhammacārino bhavissantīti ayaṃ ettha bhagavato adhippāyo.
parimuccitukāmā.example_2: ye duggatīhi parimuccitukāmā bhavissanti, te dhammacārino bhavissantīti ayaṃ ettha bhagavato adhippāyo.

aṭṭiyitukāmā.meaning_2: wishing to be troubled (by); wanting to be afflicted (by)
aṭṭiyitukāmā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of aṭṭiyati (be troubled, be afflicted) + kāma. Nominative plural agreeing with ye; the object jarāmaraṇena is instrumental.
aṭṭiyitukāmā.example_1: ye jarāmaraṇena aṭṭiyitukāmā bhavissanti, te bhavissanti bhojane mattaññuno indriyesu guttadvārā pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogamanuyuttā vipassakā kusalesu dhammesu sagāravā ca sabrahmacārīsu theresu navesu majjhimesūti ayaṃ ettha bhagavato adhippāyo.

yañcāha.meaning_2: and what I; and whatever I
yañcāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ + ca + ahaṃ (or yaṃ + ca + aha); the final -aṃ assimilates to -ā before ahaṃ. Occurs in Nettippakaraṇa prose introducing a quotation. Sometimes resolved simply as yaṃ + ca + aha.
yañcāha.example_2: yañcāha ratto atthaṃ na jānāti, ratto dhammaṃ na passatīti, imehi padehi pariyuṭṭhānehi sāyeva taṇhā abhilapitā.

paḷighañca.meaning_2: bar; crossbar; bolt (of a gate); obstacle
paḷighañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written palighañca in the text; the spelling paḷigha is a variant noted by the editors. Joined with ca, so the entry is for paligha. Accusative singular, part of the phrase sandānaṃ palighañca, 'the chain and the bar' (obstacles to be overcome).
paḷighañca.example_1: ‘‘ Yassa papañcā ṭhitī ca natthi, sandānaṃ palighañca [paḷighañca (sī.) passa udā.67] vītivatto;
paḷighañca.translation_1: “The one who has no proliferations or persistences, and has transcended the chain and the bar;

saṃsandayitvā.meaning_2: having connected; having joined together; having compared
saṃsandayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā from the causative saṃsandeti. In the text it means 'having connected (sutta with sutta)'.
saṃsandayitvā.example_1: evaṃ suttena suttaṃ saṃsandayitvā pubbāparena saddhiṃ yojayitvā suttaṃ niddiṭṭhaṃ bhavati.

sampaṭivedhena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text: 'by (his) full comprehension'. Cf. sampaṭivijjhati. The PEU entry reads it adverbially as 'thoroughly comprehending'.
sampaṭivedhena.example_1: tattha yo tividho taṇhāmūlako pamādo anuppannānaṃ bhogānaṃ uppādāya pariyesati, uppannānaṃ bhogānaṃ ārakkhaṇañca karoti paribhoganimittañca, tassa sampaṭivedhena rakkhaṇā paṭisaṃharaṇā, ayaṃ samatho.

thomanahetuvā.meaning_2: because of praise; on account of laudation
thomanahetuvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text (thomanahetuvā), with -vā as sandhi for -vā. Part of the phrase āyācanahetu vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikaṃ anuparisakkanahetu vā. thomana is from √thu 3 (praise).
thomanahetuvā.example_1: taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, api nu so puriso mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetuvā pañjalikaṃ anuparisakkanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyā”ti.
thomanahetuvā.example_2: Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, api nu so puriso mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetuvā pañjalikaṃ [pañjalikā saṃ. ni.4.358] anuparisakkanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyā ’’ ti.
thomanahetuvā.translation_2: “What do you think, village chief, might there be for that man, because of that large assembly of people’s begging, because of their imploring, or because of their beseeching with their hands joined in reverential salutation, that with the breakup of the body, after death, he would reappear in a pleasant destination, a heavenly realm?”

avaṃgaccha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for adho gaccha; found in the Sinhalese and Burmese editions. Impersonal imperative, addressed to the ghee and oil in the simile. Sandhi of avaṃ + gaccha, or possibly a clipped form of avaṃ gacchati.
avaṃgaccha.example_1: Tamenaṃ mahājanakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya ‘ osīda, bho sappitela, saṃsīda, bho sappitela, adho gaccha [avaṃgaccha (sī. ka.)]‘ bho sappitelā ’ ti.
avaṃgaccha.translation_1: Then a large assembly of people met and came together and they begged and implored and beseeched with their hands joined in reverential salutation: ‘Oh sirs, let the ghee, the oil, sink! Oh sirs, let the ghee, the oil, go down! Oh sirs, let the ghee, the oil, go downward!’”

nisevitabbā.meaning_2: to be associated with; to be practised; to be resorted to; to be indulged in
nisevitabbā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle in -tabba from nisevati (ni + √sev). Nominative singular masculine parallel to bhuñjitabbā etc. in the quotation.
nisevitabbā.example_1: ye ca kho keci evamāhaṃsu “bhuñjitabbā kāmā, paribhuñjitabbā kāmā, āsevitabbā kāmā, nisevitabbā kāmā, bhāvayitabbā kāmā, bahulīkātabbā kāmā”ti.

atthanipphattipaṭipālanā.meaning_2: guarding of the accomplishment of the goal; preserving the fulfilment of the benefit
atthanipphattipaṭipālanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of attha + nipphatti + paṭipālanā. Part of a list of terms in the Nettippakaraṇa. Nominative singular in the text.
atthanipphattipaṭipālanā.example_1: atthanipphattipaṭipālanā abhinandanā nāma, piyaṃ vā ñātiṃ abhinandati, piyaṃ vā dhammaṃ abhinandati, appaṭikūlato vā abhinandati.

adhigatappaṭisambhido.meaning_2: who has attained the discriminations; who has reached the analytical knowledges
adhigatappaṭisambhido.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Epithet of the Buddha in the buddhānussati list. In the text it stands in the nominative singular, in apposition to the subject; adhigata is a past participle of adhigacchati.
adhigatappaṭisambhido.example_1: balanipphattigato vesārajjappatto adhigatappaṭisambhido catuyogavippahīno agatigamanavītivatto uddhaṭasallo nirūḷhavaṇo madditakaṇḍako nibbāpitapariyuṭṭhāno bandhanātīto ganthaviniveṭhano ajjhāsayavītivatto bhinnandhakāro cakkhumā lokadhammasamatikkanto anurodhavirodhavippayutto iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu dhammesu asaṅkhepagato bandhanātivatto ṭhapitasaṅgāmo abhikkantataro ukkādharo ālokakaro pajjotakaro tamonudo raṇañjaho aparimāṇavaṇṇo appameyyavaṇṇo asaṅkheyyavaṇṇo ābhaṅkaro pabhaṅkaro dhammobhāsapajjotakaroti ca buddhā bhagavantoti ca buddhānussatiyā etaṃ vevacanaṃ.
adhigatappaṭisambhido.example_2: Balanipphattigato vesārajjappatto adhigatappaṭisambhido catuyogavippahīno agatigamanavītivatto uddhaṭasallo nirūḷhavaṇo madditakaṇḍako nibbāpitapariyuṭṭhāno [nibbāhita …(ka.)] bandhanātīto ganthaviniveṭhano ajjhāsayavītivatto bhinnandhakāro cakkhumā lokadhammasamatikkanto anurodhavirodhavippayutto iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu dhammesu asaṅkhepagato bandhanātivatto ṭhapitasaṅgāmo abhikkantataro ukkādharo ālokakaro pajjotakaro tamonudo raṇañjaho aparimāṇavaṇṇo appameyyavaṇṇo asaṅkheyyavaṇṇo ābhaṃkaro pabhaṃkaro dhammobhāsapajjotakaroti ca buddhā bhagavantoti ca buddhānussatiyā etaṃ vevacanaṃ.
adhigatappaṭisambhido.translation_2: And further: “He who has come to produce the Powers, reached the kinds of Intrepidity, arrived at the Discriminations, left behind the four bonds, passed beyond going the bad ways, extracted the barbs, cured the wounds, crushed the thorns, remedied the obsessions, outstripped the tether, unknotted the ties, passed beyond inclination, disrupted darkness; who is the possessor of eyesight, who has surmounted the worldly ideas, who is dissociated from favouring and opposing among wished-for and unwished-for ideas, who has no recourse to amassing, who has passed beyond the tether, who has done with battling, who is the most eminent, who is the torch-bearer, light-maker, illuminator, gloom-dispeller, renouncer of conflict, measureless in qualities, immense in qualities, incalculable in qualities, maker of radiance, maker of irradiance, illuminator of the True Ideal, enlightened, blessed.” These are synonyms for the Recollection of the Enlightened One.

nirūḷhavaṇo.meaning_2: whose wound is healed; cured of the wound
nirūḷhavaṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Epithet of the Buddha in the Buddhānussati list. nirūḷha is the past participle of nirūhati (√ruh with nir-), 'healed, cured'; vaṇa is 'wound'. Nom sg in the text.
nirūḷhavaṇo.example_1: balanipphattigato vesārajjappatto adhigatappaṭisambhido catuyogavippahīno agatigamanavītivatto uddhaṭasallo nirūḷhavaṇo madditakaṇḍako nibbāpitapariyuṭṭhāno bandhanātīto ganthaviniveṭhano ajjhāsayavītivatto bhinnandhakāro cakkhumā lokadhammasamatikkanto anurodhavirodhavippayutto iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu dhammesu asaṅkhepagato bandhanātivatto ṭhapitasaṅgāmo abhikkantataro ukkādharo ālokakaro pajjotakaro tamonudo raṇañjaho aparimāṇavaṇṇo appameyyavaṇṇo asaṅkheyyavaṇṇo ābhaṅkaro pabhaṅkaro dhammobhāsapajjotakaroti ca buddhā bhagavantoti ca buddhānussatiyā etaṃ vevacanaṃ.
nirūḷhavaṇo.example_2: Balanipphattigato vesārajjappatto adhigatappaṭisambhido catuyogavippahīno agatigamanavītivatto uddhaṭasallo nirūḷhavaṇo madditakaṇḍako nibbāpitapariyuṭṭhāno [nibbāhita …(ka.)] bandhanātīto ganthaviniveṭhano ajjhāsayavītivatto bhinnandhakāro cakkhumā lokadhammasamatikkanto anurodhavirodhavippayutto iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu dhammesu asaṅkhepagato bandhanātivatto ṭhapitasaṅgāmo abhikkantataro ukkādharo ālokakaro pajjotakaro tamonudo raṇañjaho aparimāṇavaṇṇo appameyyavaṇṇo asaṅkheyyavaṇṇo ābhaṃkaro pabhaṃkaro dhammobhāsapajjotakaroti ca buddhā bhagavantoti ca buddhānussatiyā etaṃ vevacanaṃ.
nirūḷhavaṇo.translation_2: And further: “He who has come to produce the Powers, reached the kinds of Intrepidity, arrived at the Discriminations, left behind the four bonds, passed beyond going the bad ways, extracted the barbs, cured the wounds, crushed the thorns, remedied the obsessions, outstripped the tether, unknotted the ties, passed beyond inclination, disrupted darkness; who is the possessor of eyesight, who has surmounted the worldly ideas, who is dissociated from favouring and opposing among wished-for and unwished-for ideas, who has no recourse to amassing, who has passed beyond the tether, who has done with battling, who is the most eminent, who is the torch-bearer, light-maker, illuminator, gloom-dispeller, renouncer of conflict, measureless in qualities, immense in qualities, incalculable in qualities, maker of radiance, maker of irradiance, illuminator of the True Ideal, enlightened, blessed.” These are synonyms for the Recollection of the Enlightened One.

ābhaṃkaro.meaning_2: radiance-making; producing light; creator of splendour
ābhaṃkaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Epithet of the Buddha. Nom. sg. in the text, but as an adjective its lemma_2 is the same. Probably a variant of ābhākara.
ābhaṃkaro.example_1: Balanipphattigato vesārajjappatto adhigatappaṭisambhido catuyogavippahīno agatigamanavītivatto uddhaṭasallo nirūḷhavaṇo madditakaṇḍako nibbāpitapariyuṭṭhāno [nibbāhita …(ka.)] bandhanātīto ganthaviniveṭhano ajjhāsayavītivatto bhinnandhakāro cakkhumā lokadhammasamatikkanto anurodhavirodhavippayutto iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu dhammesu asaṅkhepagato bandhanātivatto ṭhapitasaṅgāmo abhikkantataro ukkādharo ālokakaro pajjotakaro tamonudo raṇañjaho aparimāṇavaṇṇo appameyyavaṇṇo asaṅkheyyavaṇṇo ābhaṃkaro pabhaṃkaro dhammobhāsapajjotakaroti ca buddhā bhagavantoti ca buddhānussatiyā etaṃ vevacanaṃ.
ābhaṃkaro.translation_1: And further: “He who has come to produce the Powers, reached the kinds of Intrepidity, arrived at the Discriminations, left behind the four bonds, passed beyond going the bad ways, extracted the barbs, cured the wounds, crushed the thorns, remedied the obsessions, outstripped the tether, unknotted the ties, passed beyond inclination, disrupted darkness; who is the possessor of eyesight, who has surmounted the worldly ideas, who is dissociated from favouring and opposing among wished-for and unwished-for ideas, who has no recourse to amassing, who has passed beyond the tether, who has done with battling, who is the most eminent, who is the torch-bearer, light-maker, illuminator, gloom-dispeller, renouncer of conflict, measureless in qualities, immense in qualities, incalculable in qualities, maker of radiance, maker of irradiance, illuminator of the True Ideal, enlightened, blessed.” These are synonyms for the Recollection of the Enlightened One.

apalokiyaṃ.meaning_2: worn away; destroyed; consumed; (variant reading for apalokita)
apalokiyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has the variant apalokiyaṃ, i.e. apalokitaṃ, accusative singular agreeing with the neuter subject; the Sinhala and Burmese editions read apalokitaṃ. Sometimes explained differently in the commentaries.
apalokiyaṃ.example_1: Ajajjaraṃ dhuvaṃ apalokitaṃ [apalokiyaṃ (sī. ka.)], anidassanaṃ nippapañca santaṃ.
apalokiyaṃ.translation_1: The ageless, everlasting, and un-worn-away, making no showing, undiversifying, at peace.”

nītikadhammameva.meaning_2: just that which is of the nature of misfortune; only what has misfortune as its nature
nītikadhammameva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of nītikadhamma (adj) and eva (emph). Variant reading in brackets in the text; the main reading is anītikadhamma. Could also be analysed as nītika + dhamma + eva.
nītikadhammameva.example_1: Anītikaṃ anītikadhammaṃ [nītikadhammameva vā (sī. ka.) passa saṃ. ni.4.409], nibbānametaṃ sugatena desitaṃ.
nītikadhammameva.translation_1: free from misfortune, whose nature it is to be unplagued: this Nibbana was taught by the Sugata.”

abhinighātapaññatti.meaning_2: concept of counteraction; notion of destruction; designation of eradication
abhinighātapaññatti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text, paired with pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ. The first member abhinighāta (from abhi + ni + √han) means striking down, counteraction, destruction.
abhinighātapaññatti.example_1: ayaṃ uppādapaññatti khaye ñāṇassa, okāsapaññatti anuppāde ñāṇassa, bhāvanāpaññatti maggassa, pariññāpaññatti dukkhassa, pahānapaññatti samudayassa, ārambhapaññatti vīriyindriyassa, āhaṭanāpaññatti āsāṭikānaṃ, nikkhepapaññatti bhāvanābhūmiyā, abhinighātapaññatti pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ.
abhinighātapaññatti.example_2: Ayaṃ uppādapaññatti khaye ñāṇassa, okāsapaññatti anuppāde ñāṇassa, bhāvanāpaññatti maggassa, pariññāpaññatti dukkhassa, pahānapaññatti samudayassa, ārambhapaññatti vīriyindriyassa, āsāṭanapaññatti āsāṭikānaṃ, nikkhepapaññatti bhāvanābhūmiyā, abhinighātapaññatti pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ.
abhinighātapaññatti.translation_2: This is a description in terms of arising applied to knowledge of exhaustion (khaye ñāṇassa), a description in terms of opportunity (okāsapaññatti) applied to knowledge of non-arising (anuppāde ñāṇassa), a description in terms of keeping in being applied to the path, a description in terms of diagnosis applied to suffering, a description in terms of abandoning applied to origin, a description in terms of instigation (ārambhapaññatti) applied to the energy faculty, a description in terms of ‘removal’ (āsāṭanapaññatti) applied to ‘grubs’ (āsāṭikānaṃ), a description in terms of presentation applied to the plane of keeping in being (bhāvanābhūmiyā), a description in terms of counteraction (abhinighātapaññatti) applied to evil unwholesome ideas (pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ).

sekkhāni.meaning_2: of a trainee; belonging to one still in training
sekkhāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is neuter plural, agreeing with pañcindriyāni: 'the five faculties of a trainee'. Analyses as sekha + ya or as a secondary adjective from sekha are also possible.
sekkhāni.example_1: “ayaṃ ahasmīti anānupassī”ti ayaṃ sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā samugghāto, sā sekkhāvimutti, tāniyeva sekkhāni pañcindriyāni.
sekkhāni.example_2: tāniyeva sekkhāni pañcindriyāni vijjā, vijjuppādā avijjānirodho, avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho, evaṃ sabbo paṭiccasamuppādo.

vipassanāvase.meaning_2: in virtue of insight; by the power of insight; on account of insight
vipassanāvase.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, in the phrase vipassanāvase, parallel to samathavasena. vasa here means power; control; dependence (cf. vasena).
vipassanāvase.example_1: ‘‘ Anissitassa calitaṃ natthī ’’ ti samathavasena vā taṇhāya anissito vipassanāvase vā diṭṭhiyā anissito.
vipassanāvase.translation_1: “The unsupported is not liable to dislodgement”: unsupported by craving in virtue of tranquility, or unsupported by view in virtue of insight.

nevidhāti.meaning_2: not in this way?; not so?
nevidhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the phrase "nevidhā"ti it is a sandhi form quoted as a term: probably na + evaṃ (or na + eva + idha). Meaning uncertain; gloss with question mark. Followed by the quotative ti.
nevidhāti.example_1: āgatigatīpi na bhavanti, “nevidhā”ti chasu ajjhattikesu āyatanesu.

nevesāhaṃ.meaning_2: not so, I; it is not thus for me
nevesāhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (sī. ka. editions) of the attested passage; the text as printed reads 'na ve sāhaṃ' (= na ve so ahaṃ), per the apparatus. Treated here as a sandhi of na + eva + ahaṃ. Sinhalese and Cambodian editions differ; the meaning in context is idiomatically 'it is not so, I (say/mean)'.
nevesāhaṃ.example_1: Tenāha bhagavā yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu [nevesāhaṃ (sī. ka.) passa ma. ni.3.349], yā ca bāhirā pathavīdhātu, pathavīdhāturevesā.
nevesāhaṃ.translation_1: Therefore, the Blessed One said: “Both the internal earth element and the external earth element are just the earth element.

saṃlakkhaṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed among synonyms of paññā in the Nettippakaraṇa; feminine form of saṃlakkhaṇa. Nominative singular.
saṃlakkhaṇā.example_1: Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ, pubbante ñāṇaṃ, aparante ñāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante ñāṇaṃ, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ, yā evarūpā paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo saṃlakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇā paṇḍiccaṃ kosallaṃ nepuññaṃ vebhabyā [vebhavyā (sī.)] cintā upaparikkhā bhūrī medhā pariṇāyikā vipassanā sampajaññaṃ patodo paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ paññāsatthaṃ paññāpāsādo paññāāloko paññāobhāso paññāpajjoto paññāratanaṃ amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ.
saṃlakkhaṇā.translation_1: It is knowledge about suffering, knowledge about the origin of suffering, knowledge about cessation of suffering, knowledge about the path leading to the cessation of suffering; knowledge about the past, knowledge about the future, knowledge about the past and future; knowledge about phenomena arisen dependent on conditions. Any such wisdom, understanding, investigation, analysis of phenomena, good observation, observation, scrutiny, discernment, skill, cleverness, elucidation, thought, scrutiny, breadth, wit, guidance, insight, awareness, goad, faculty of wisdom, strength of wisdom, weapon of wisdom, palace of wisdom, light of wisdom, illumination of wisdom, brightness of wisdom, jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, right view, investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, path factor, included in the path.

vebhavyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant vebhavyā is given in the text; the main form vebhabyā is also attested. It appears in a long list of synonyms for wisdom (paññā).
vebhavyā.example_1: Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ, pubbante ñāṇaṃ, aparante ñāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante ñāṇaṃ, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ, yā evarūpā paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo saṃlakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇā paṇḍiccaṃ kosallaṃ nepuññaṃ vebhabyā [vebhavyā (sī.)] cintā upaparikkhā bhūrī medhā pariṇāyikā vipassanā sampajaññaṃ patodo paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ paññāsatthaṃ paññāpāsādo paññāāloko paññāobhāso paññāpajjoto paññāratanaṃ amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ.
vebhavyā.translation_1: It is knowledge about suffering, knowledge about the origin of suffering, knowledge about cessation of suffering, knowledge about the path leading to the cessation of suffering; knowledge about the past, knowledge about the future, knowledge about the past and future; knowledge about phenomena arisen dependent on conditions. Any such wisdom, understanding, investigation, analysis of phenomena, good observation, observation, scrutiny, discernment, skill, cleverness, elucidation, thought, scrutiny, breadth, wit, guidance, insight, awareness, goad, faculty of wisdom, strength of wisdom, weapon of wisdom, palace of wisdom, light of wisdom, illumination of wisdom, brightness of wisdom, jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, right view, investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, path factor, included in the path.

āgaḷhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it occurs in the compound āgaḷhapaṭipadā ('intense practice'), glossed āgāḷhapaṭipadā in the sī. quotation; printed as a separate word next to paṭipadā. Possibly a byform of āgāḷha from √gāh (dive, plunge).
āgaḷhā.example_1: Āgāḷhapaṭipadā [āgaḷhā paṭipadā (sī.) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā], nijjhāmapaṭipadā, majjhimapaṭipadā, akkhamā paṭipadā, khamā paṭipadā, samā paṭipadā, damā paṭipadā, dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā, dukkhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā, sukhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā, sukhā paṭipadā khippābhiññāti.
āgaḷhā.translation_1: There is luxurious practice, austere practice, the middle way practice; intolerant practice, tolerant practice, even practice, self-controlled practice; practice that is painful with slow intuition, practice that is painful with quick intuition, practice that is pleasant with slow intuition, practice that is pleasant with quick intuition.

ekī.meaning_2: one; united; of one nature; single
ekī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Predicate adjective with bhavati ('bhavati ekī'), agreeing with dhammo; ekī here means 'becomes one (with)', 'is unified'. Sometimes analysed as eka + ī suffix. Not a verb form.
ekī.example_1: evaṃ yo dhammo yassa dhammassa samānabhāvo, so dhammo tassa dhammassa ekattatāya ekī bhavati.

vilakkhaṇo.meaning_2: having different characteristics; with different signs; distinct; diverse
vilakkhaṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Masculine nominative singular in the text. Describes something that varies according to its distinguishing marks.
vilakkhaṇo.example_1: yena yena vā pana vilakkhaṇo, tena tena vemattaṃ gacchati.

avupacchedattho.meaning_2: meaning of non-interruption; sense of continuity
avupacchedattho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative or nominative singular in the text; glosses santati attho. Probably a + vupaccheda + attha (non-cutting-off), though avu- is doubtful.
avupacchedattho.example_1: avupacchedattho santati attho, nibbatti attho phalattho, paṭisandhi attho punabbhavattho, palibodhattho pariyuṭṭhānattho, asamugghātattho anusayattho, asampaṭivedhattho avijjattho, apariññātattho viññāṇassa bījattho.

asampaṭivedhattho.meaning_2: state of not penetrating; nature of not comprehending
asampaṭivedhattho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound; first member asampaṭivedha (a + sampaṭivedha, from √vid). Nominative singular in the text, listing defilements (avijjā).
asampaṭivedhattho.example_1: avupacchedattho santati attho, nibbatti attho phalattho, paṭisandhi attho punabbhavattho, palibodhattho pariyuṭṭhānattho, asamugghātattho anusayattho, asampaṭivedhattho avijjattho, apariññātattho viññāṇassa bījattho.

avupacchedo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + upaccheda (na + upa- + cheda), written avupaccheda; the PEU split as Na+upaccheda agrees. Nominative singular in the text, in the formula yattha ... tattha santati.
avupacchedo.example_1: yattha avupacchedo tattha santati, yattha santati tattha nibbatti, yattha nibbatti tattha phalaṃ, yattha phalaṃ tattha paṭisandhi, yattha paṭisandhi tattha punabbhavo, yattha punabbhavo tattha palibodho, yattha palibodho tattha pariyuṭṭhānaṃ, yattha pariyuṭṭhānaṃ tattha asamugghāto.

asampaṭivedho.meaning_2: lack of understanding; non-penetration; failure to realise
asampaṭivedho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Nettippakaraṇa this is a link in a chain of conditions: where there is no penetration (of the truth), there is ignorance. Nominative singular in the text.
asampaṭivedho.example_1: yattha asamugghāto tattha anusayo, yattha anusayo tattha asampaṭivedho, yattha asampaṭivedho tattha avijjā, yattha avijjā tattha sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ apariññātaṃ, yattha sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ apariññātaṃ tattha bījattho.

yaṃmūlā.meaning_2: having which as root; whose root is whatever
yaṃmūlā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Relative clause: yaṃ + mūlā, 'those phenomena of which (yaṃ) are the roots (mūlā)'. Plural nominative agreeing with dhammā. In the quotation 'ye dhammā yaṃmūlā ...'.
yaṃmūlā.example_2: “ye dhammā yaṃmūlā, ye cekatthā pakāsitā muninā”ti.

rūpupikā.meaning_2: form-station (of consciousness); station of consciousness connected with form
rūpupikā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of rūpūpikā (rūpa + upaya); in the text it qualifies viññāṇaṭṭhiti, abl. sg. rūpūpikāya understood. See PEU rūpupaya.
rūpupikā.example_1: Kāye kāyānupassī viharanto ‘‘ asubhe subhan ’’ ti vipallāsaṃ pajahati, kabaḷīkāro cassa āhāro pariññaṃ gacchati, kāmupādānena ca anupādāno bhavati, kāmayogena ca visaṃyutto bhavati, abhijjhākāyaganthena ca vippayujjati, kāmāsavena ca anāsavo bhavati, kāmoghañca uttiṇṇo bhavati, rāgasallena ca visallo bhavati, rūpūpikā [rūpupikā (ka.) evamuparipi] cassa viññāṇaṭṭhiti pariññaṃ gacchati, rūpadhātuyaṃ cassa rāgo pahīno bhavati, na ca chandāgatiṃ gacchati.
rūpupikā.translation_1: One who abides contemplating the body as a body abandons the perversion that there is beauty in the ugly; his physical nutriment comes within his full understanding; he is without clinging in regard to sensual-desire clinging; he is unfettered in regard to the bond of sensual desire; he is dissociated in regard to the bodily tie of covetousness; he is free of taints in regard to the taint of sensual desire; he has crossed over the flood of sensual desire; he is barbless as regards the barb of lust; the station for consciousness of form comes within his full understanding; his lust for the form element is abandoned; and he does not take a wrong course because of desire.

vipallāsayati.meaning_2: perverts; distorts; corrupts; turns upside down; misrepresents
vipallāsayati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of vi + pari + √as, lit. 'causes to be reversed'. 3rd singular in the text; questions about what (kiṃ) and where (kuhiṃ) one distorts. PEU connects it with vipallāsa ('perversion, inversion').

vipallāsīyati.meaning_2: is perverted; is distorted; is corrupted
vipallāsīyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive/causative form; text has vipallāsīyati in the present tense, 3rd singular. The PEU suggests a causative sense.
vipallāsīyati.example_1: taṇhānivutaṃ cittaṃ dvīhi vipallāsehi vipallāsīyati “asubhe subhan”ti “dukkhe sukhan”ti.
vipallāsīyati.example_2: diṭṭhinivutaṃ cittaṃ dvīhi vipallāsehi vipallāsīyati “anicce niccan”ti “anattani attā”ti.

pītipharaṇo.meaning_2: suffused with joy; pervaded by delight
pītipharaṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular masculine, agreeing with a subject such as samatha or a person. The related entry pītipharaṇa is a neuter noun meaning 'suffusion with delight'; pītipharaṇo could also be analysed as a noun in apposition.
pītipharaṇo.example_1: tattha yo ca pītipharaṇo yo ca sukhapharaṇo yo ca cetopharaṇo, ayaṃ samatho.

sukhapharaṇo.meaning_2: pervaded by happiness; suffused with ease
sukhapharaṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of sukha and pharaṇa. In the text it is nominative singular masculine, modifying an unstated subject (the meditative state).
sukhapharaṇo.example_1: tattha yo ca pītipharaṇo yo ca sukhapharaṇo yo ca cetopharaṇo, ayaṃ samatho.

cetopharaṇo.meaning_2: pervading the mind; suffusing the mind
cetopharaṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular masculine modifying an implied subject (samatha or the person). The related entry gives neuter (na), but here it agrees with a masculine noun.
cetopharaṇo.example_1: tattha yo ca pītipharaṇo yo ca sukhapharaṇo yo ca cetopharaṇo, ayaṃ samatho.

abhinibbidhā.meaning_2: breaking open; shattering; (the insight or path that) breaks through
abhinibbidhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text has abhinibbidhā (with dh), a variant spelling of abhinibbidā; nominative singular fem, object of na ... bhabbo ... gantuṃ ('not able to go to ...'). Cf. PEU's Abhinibbhidā. Doubt: root and formation are uncertain; possibly derived from abhinibbijjhati (√bhid). Meaning here seems to be the breaking through / tearing apart of defilements, i.e. path insight.
abhinibbidhā.example_1: yaṃ evaṃ jātiyaṃ kammasamādānaṃ, iminā puggalena akusalakammasamādānaṃ upacitaṃ avipakkaṃ vipākāya paccupaṭṭhitaṃ na ca bhabbo abhinibbidhā gantunti taṃ bhagavā na ovadati.

āvārayissati.meaning_2: will obstruct; will block; will hinder
āvārayissati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Future 3rd singular of āvārayati (causative of āvarati, 'to obstruct'); in the text it refers to the arising of unwholesome kamma obstructing the path.
āvārayissati.example_1: imassa ca puggalassa akusalakammasamādānaṃ paripūramānaṃ maggaṃ āvārayissati purā pāripūriṃ gacchati, purā phalaṃ nibbattayati, purā maggamāvārayati, purā veneyyattaṃ samatikkamatīti taṃ bhagavā asamattaṃ ovadati.

paripālīyatīti.meaning_2: is protected; is guarded; is maintained
paripālīyatīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text this is part of the quotation paripālīyatīti, where -ti is the quotative and belongs to the following iti; the verb is passive-looking but classed as a causative formation of pariharati. See paripālīyati in the wider context of nirutti.

padosayitvā.meaning_2: having corrupted; having made (one's mind) bad (towards); having spoiled
padosayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative padoseti (padūseti), 'to corrupt, spoil (the mind)'. Used with cittaṃ and a locative of the person: 'having harboured an evil thought towards'. The PEU's 'ṇaya' appears to be an error for the causative -e-.
padosayitvā.example_1: kokāliko hi sāriputtamoggallānesu theresu cittaṃ padosayitvā mahāpadumaniraye upapanno.

sampaṭivedho.meaning_2: thorough comprehension; full penetration; direct understanding
sampaṭivedho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text, listed with abhisamaya and saccāgamana as aspects of right view. PEU suggests √vidh, but the sense fits √vid 1 (know); the -vedha suffix is irregular either way.
sampaṭivedho.example_1: sammādiṭṭhi nāma yaṃ dukkhe ñāṇaṃ dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ magge ñāṇaṃ hetumhi ñāṇaṃ hetusamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ paccaye ñāṇaṃ paccayasamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ, yaṃ tattha tattha yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ abhisamayo sampaṭivedho saccāgamanaṃ, ayaṃ vemattatā.

ummujjanimujjāni.meaning_2: rising and sinking; rising up and being submerged; bobbing up and down
ummujjanimujjāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural in the text (nominative or accusative); part of the phrase ummujjanimujjāni karontā, expressing repeatedly surfacing and sinking in the lower realms.
ummujjanimujjāni.example_1: yo kāme paṭisevati, so lokaṃ vaḍḍhayati, yo lokaṃ vaḍḍhayati, so bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavatīti te evaṃsaññī evaṃdiṭṭhī dukkhena sukhaṃ patthayamānā kāmesu puññasaññī attakilamathānuyogamanuyuttā ca viharanti kāmasukhallikānuyogamanuyuttā ca, te tadabhiññā santā rogameva vaḍḍhayanti, gaṇḍameva vaḍḍhayanti, sallameva vaḍḍhayanti, te rogābhitunnā gaṇḍapaṭipīḷitā sallānuviddhā nirayatiracchānayonipetāsuresu ummujjanimujjāni karontā ugghātanigghātaṃ paccanubhontā rogagaṇḍasallabhesajjaṃ na vindanti.

anādianidhanappavattaṃ.meaning_2: without beginning or end; beginningless and endless; continuing without start or finish
anādianidhanappavattaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes the net of wrong views (mohajālaṃ). Nominative singular neuter agreeing with mohajālaṃ; written here as one compound.

tetālīsaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of tecattālīsaṃ in the text; the number 43, agreeing with bodhipakkhiyā dhammā. The PEU entry treats tetālīsa as an ordinal; if taken as a cardinal it agrees with the plural subject.
tetālīsaṃ.translation_1: The forty-three factors partaking of enlightenment are the diamond of knowledge that bursts open the web of delusion.

viveciyamāno.meaning_2: being separated (from); being secluded (from); discrete; being kept apart
viveciyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive sense 'being separated'. The form is the present participle of the causative vivecayati; the passive intensive ending -iyamāna is due to the causative stem. Nominative singular agreeing with 'so'. The verb takes the ablative or instrumental of separation (kāmehi).
viveciyamāno.example_1: tattha kiṅkāraṇaṃ, yaṃ taṇhācarito dukkhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya khippābhiññāya ca niyyāti, tassa hi kāmā apariccattā bhavanti, so kāmehi viveciyamāno dukkhena paṭinissarati dandhañca dhammaṃ ājānāti?
viveciyamāno.example_2: so tato viveciyamāno khippañca paṭinissarati, khippañca dhammaṃ ājānāti.

udatthassa.meaning_2: of noble mind; one whose mind is noble; noble and wise person
udatthassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Siamese and Burmese editions read udattassa. Genitive singular in the text, qualifying diṭṭhicaritassa. Alternative analysis udattha = ud + attha, 'of high purpose'.
udatthassa.translation_1: These are the imperfections in a person of intelligent view-temperament.

disalocanenāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is quoted as “oloketvā disalocanenā”ti, with the following word disalocanena and the quotative -ti attached to it; here the entry is made for the absolutive oloketvā.
disalocanenāti.example_1: tenāha “yo akusale samūlehi netī”ti “oloketvā disalocanenā”ti ca.

bhagīnisu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text (bhagīnisu); the form is instrumental/locative plural of bhaginī. Here it refers respectfully to female renunciants, sisters.
bhagīnisu.example_1: Na kho pana mayaṃ, bhante, abhijānāma tāsu bhagīnisu pāpakaṃ cittaṃ ñappādentā, ayaṃ kho no, bhante, etamhā sambādhā añño sambādho sambādhataro ceva sambādhasaṅghātataro cāti.
bhagīnisu.translation_1: Yet, venerable sir, we do not confess to generating an evil mind toward those sisters. This, venerable sir, is our other constraint more constraining and counted more constraining than that constraint of the household life.”

okkā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these verses okkā appears to be a poetic word for radiance or a flame-like light issuing from the mouth; related to ukkā. Nominative singular.
okkā.translation_2: a thousand rays like lightning, a splendour came forth from his mouth.

pasāsiya.meaning_2: having ruled; having governed; having administered; having ordered
pasāsiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -iya (variant of -itvā), here governing rajjaṃ: 'having ruled the kingdom'. The PEU analysis pa + sāsa + tvā (bya) agrees. The form is also metrically usable in verse, as in the Nettippakaraṇa quotation.
pasāsiya.translation_2: “‘“And after ruling godly blessings and celestial realms among the devas,

vidhūtalatoti.meaning_2: with (view) wrongness shaken off; (lit.) having shaken off the creeper
vidhūtalatoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular with -ti (quotation) joined; read vidhūtalatāya. Orthography suggests latoti = latā + ti.

āsihi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Future 3rd singular of atthi, formed on the √as- base (not bhavissati). The sandhi āsihi = āsi + i? Doubtful; possibly āsi (aorist of atthi?) or a misreading. Occurs in the phrase samāgamo āsihi.
āsihi.example_1: Imehi me antimadehadhāribhi, samāgamo āsihi tāhi tāsihi.
āsihi.translation_1: I have had a meeting with these private Buddhas who have crossed beyond both woe and weal and bear their final body.

avocābhipasannacitto.meaning_2: with a mind of firm confidence, he said
avocābhipasannacitto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of avoca (aorist of vadati) + abhipasannacitta in the nominative singular. The second word is a compound abhi + pasanna + citta.
avocābhipasannacitto.example_2: ‘‘ So maṃ avocābhipasannacitto, tuyhameva etaṃ pupphaṃ dadāmi;
avocābhipasannacitto.translation_2: “With a mind of firm confidence, he said to me: ‘I give this single flower to you as a gift.’

addasiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular aorist, used with the emphatic pronoun sohaṃ (so + ahaṃ). Formally identical to the aorist stem addasi- with the 1sg ending -ṃ.
addasiṃ.translation_2: I saw the Sambuddha, Upariṭṭha of holy fame.

orūhitvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvāna of orūhati (ava + √ruh); used with the ablative pāsādā. The initial o- represents the prefix ava/o.
orūhitvāna.translation_2: I descended from my mansion and approached the Sambuddha Gotama.

māvidha.meaning_2: O Māvidha; name of a person addressed (Māgandiya)
māvidha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative address in verse ('do not, sir!'); perhaps a sandhi of mā + idha ('not here'), but the metre and the parallel in Sn 4.13 suggest a vocative proper name (variant reading Māgandiya).
māvidha.example_2: ‘‘ Sukhaṃ sayanti munayo, na te socanti māvidha;
māvidha.translation_2: “Sages sleep happily; they do not sorrow here, Māvidha,

viveciyamānena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive present participle viveciyamāna; instrumental singular in the text, 'even by one being excluded'.
viveciyamānena.example_1: “sattahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ kalyāṇamittaṃ api viveciyamānena paṇāmiyamānena gale pisanamajjamānena yāvajīvaṃ na vijahitabbaṃ.
viveciyamānena.example_2: ‘‘ Sattahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ kalyāṇamittaṃ api viveciyamānena paṇāmiyamānena gale pisanamajjamānena [galepi pamajjamānena (sī.)] yāvajīvaṃ na vijahitabbaṃ.
viveciyamānena.translation_2: “Monks, a good friend endowed with seven factors should never be abandoned as long as life lasts, even if one is being excluded, dismissed, or even seized by the neck and driven away.

yimaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written yimaṃ after na for sandhi; the word is imaṃ, accusative singular of ima. Matched with lokaṃ.
yimaṃ.example_1: Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, dīgharattaṃ katānaṃ puññānaṃ iṭṭhaṃ [dīgharattaṃ iṭṭhaṃ (sī. ka.) passa itivu.22] kantaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ vipākaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ, satta vassāni mettacittaṃ bhāvetvā satta saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe na imaṃ [na yimaṃ (itivu.22)] lokaṃ punarāgamāsiṃ.
yimaṃ.translation_1: I confess, monks, having for a long time experienced the wished-for, desired, dear, and agreeable result of merit performed; for seven years I maintained a mind of loving-kindness, and for seven eons of involution and evolution I never came back to this world.

disoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The -ti is the ordinary 3rd singular ending, not the quotative ti; diso is the 3rd singular present of √dis with o from a + ti. The sentence is metrical. Alternative analysis: diso ti = disā + iti, but the quotation marks support a verb.

jotirivindhanakkhayā.meaning_2: like a fire with its fuel exhausted; as a light goes out when the fuel is used up
jotirivindhanakkhayā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentarial-style simile: joti + iva + indhana + khaya. Included in the quotation 'nibbanti te jotirivindhanakkhayā'. Idealy analysed as joti iva (indhanassa) khayā, 'like a flame because of the exhaustion of fuel'.
jotirivindhanakkhayā.example_2: Khayā ca kammassa vimuttacetaso, nibbanti te jotirivindhanakkhayā ’’.
jotirivindhanakkhayā.translation_2: with the destruction of kamma, those with hearts liberated reach extinguishment like lamps with fuel all used up.”

vuṭṭhiveparamā.meaning_2: having Nibbāna as the highest; with Nibbāna as the ultimate
vuṭṭhiveparamā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vuṭṭhi (Nibbāna) + veparamā (having as the highest). Appears in the verse 'Natthi paññāsamā ābhā, vuṭṭhiveparamā sarā'. Alternative split: vuṭṭhi + eparamā.
vuṭṭhiveparamā.example_2: Natthi paññāsamā ābhā, vuṭṭhiveparamā sarā ’’ ti.
vuṭṭhiveparamā.translation_2: there is no radiance equal to wisdom, the rain is indeed the greatest of pools.”

bhikkhaveऋ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form bhikkhaveऋ contains a stray Devanagari character; taken as bhikkhave, the vocative plural of bhikkhu, used when addressing monks.

nirupadāho.meaning_2: without conflict; free from trouble; without burning (of defilements)
nirupadāho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The PEU entry gives it as a ti (adjective) meaning \'free from the burning of lust\'. In the Nettippakaraṇa it describes the Dhamma as entirely without conflict or affliction. The form is nominative singular masculine.
nirupadāho.example_2: ‘‘ Satthā ca appaṭisamo, dhammo ca sabbo nirupadāho;
nirupadāho.translation_2: “The Teacher is peerless, and the entire Dhamma is without conflict;

asādhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text as asādhā, probably a sandhi or compound fragment (sādhāraṇe asādhā-); the reading and analysis are uncertain. If taken as a nominative plural of asādhu, the form would be asādhū, so asādhā may belong to a different compound or be a scribal variant.
